title: Understanding 401k Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs) Without Jargon
bigPicture: Once you hit age 73, the government requires you to take some money out of your 401k every year — think of it as your long-overdue tax bill.
whatYouNeedToKnow: You must start taking RMDs at age 73 (was 70½ before recent law changes).
The amount is based on your account balance and your life expectancy — bigger balance means bigger withdrawal.
Missing your RMD triggers a steep 25% penalty on the amount you should have taken.
Roth 401k accounts now also require RMDs, but you can avoid this by rolling funds into a Roth IRA.
You can take your RMD in one lump sum or spread it across the year — your choice.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Forgetting to take your RMD by December 31 (or April 1 for your first year — but that backfires and gives you two withdrawals one year).
Guessing the amount instead of using the IRS worksheet or your plan provider's calculator.
Thinking you can skip RMDs if you're still working — that only applies to your current employer's plan if you own less than 5%.
Taking too little and facing the 25% penalty.
actionSteps: Check your 401k statement each October to see if you've started receiving RMD notices from your plan provider.
Use the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table or an online RMD calculator to figure out your exact amount.
Set a calendar reminder for December 1st each year so you don't miss the deadline.
Talk to a tax advisor before your first RMD year to plan around taxes and income.
